limit.description: Max items to return (1-25, default 25). Combine with offset to page through a truncated list.

name: cerberus_resource_status
description: Get runtime status for one resource. Read artifact_stale and recommended_action / recommended_next_step and act on them — or just call cerberus_resource_ensure_fresh to perform the recommended action automatically. Use before deploy, apply, reload, or remove.

name: cerberus_resource_inspect
description: Get runtime details, install paths, and log paths for one resource.

name: cerberus_resource_doctor
description: Run checks for one resource and return pass, warn, or fail guidance.

name: cerberus_resource_logs
description: Get recent logs for one resource.

approval_id.description: The approval id from an approval_pending answer, once your operator has approved it. Retry with exactly the same arguments; anything different is plan_stale.

lines.description: Number of lines to return. Default 50.

name: cerberus_resource_reload
description: Restart an installed resource WITHOUT rebuilding or syncing — relaunches the existing (possibly stale) artifact. If the source changed, use cerberus_resource_deploy or cerberus_resource_ensure_fresh with force=true instead. Requires acknowledged=true.

acknowledged.description: Acknowledge the operation. Required: every resource mutation needs it.

approval_id.description: The approval id from an approval_pending answer, once your operator has approved it. Retry with exactly the same arguments; anything different is plan_stale.

name: cerberus_resource_stop
description: Stop a resource without uninstalling it. Use remove for uninstall. Requires acknowledged=true.

acknowledged.description: Acknowledge the operation. Required: every resource mutation needs it.

approval_id.description: The approval id from an approval_pending answer, once your operator has approved it. Retry with exactly the same arguments; anything different is plan_stale.

name: cerberus_resource_deploy
description: Build, sync, and apply a resource from the current source tree. Use this when source changed and you want the running service to match it — run_from: artifact services run an installed copy, so building (go/make) or reloading alone does NOT update them. This is the default action after editing source. ensure_fresh requires force=true to guarantee a rebuild. Requires acknowledged=true.

acknowledged.description: Acknowledge the operation. Required: every resource mutation needs it.

approval_id.description: The approval id from an approval_pending answer, once your operator has approved it. Retry with exactly the same arguments; anything different is plan_stale.

name: cerberus_resource_ensure_fresh
description: Reconcile drift between built binaries and installed/running resources. Source edits are NOT checked. After editing source, use cerberus_resource_deploy or pass force=true to rebuild, install and activate. Without force, this may apply/sync existing binaries or report no built-binary drift. Unconfirmed activation returns success=false without restarting; follow the verification guidance before retrying. Requires acknowledged=true.

acknowledged.description: Acknowledge the operation. Required: every resource mutation needs it.

approval_id.description: The approval id from an approval_pending answer, once your operator has approved it. Retry with exactly the same arguments; anything different is plan_stale.

force.description: Always rebuild, install and activate. Required after source edits in ANY runtime mode; default false only checks built-binary drift.

name: cerberus_resource_sync
description: Sync installed artifacts without applying the runtime backend. Requires acknowledged=true.

acknowledged.description: Acknowledge the operation. Required: every resource mutation needs it.

approval_id.description: The approval id from an approval_pending answer, once your operator has approved it. Retry with exactly the same arguments; anything different is plan_stale.

name: cerberus_resource_apply
description: Activate an already-built resource WITHOUT running its build step. If the source changed, use cerberus_resource_deploy (or cerberus_resource_ensure_fresh with force=true) so it rebuilds first. Requires acknowledged=true.

acknowledged.description: Acknowledge the operation. Required: every resource mutation needs it.

approval_id.description: The approval id from an approval_pending answer, once your operator has approved it. Retry with exactly the same arguments; anything different is plan_stale.

name: cerberus_lockdown
description: Put Cerberus in lockdown: every operation but a plain read is refused until a person lifts it. Use it when you believe you, or something acting through Cerberus, is doing harm, and say why. You cannot lift it; a person does, with `cerberus lockdown --off`.

name: cerberus_host_list
description: List declared hosts with recorded state and probed facts (budgeted envelope). Each host reports state, probed_at and stale; stale or never-probed hosts are called out in the text. Facts only: hosts are in name order, not ranked.

labels.description: Only hosts with all of these labels.

limit.description: Max items to return (1-25, default 25). Combine with offset to page through a truncated list.

offset.description: Number of items to skip before this page (default 0). Use with limit to page through results.

role.description: Only hosts with this declared role.

name: cerberus_host_get
description: Show one declared host: declared specs and probed facts side by side, state, probed_at and stale.

name: cerberus_host_probe
description: Measure one host over ssh with a fixed read-only script and record the facts. An unreachable host is reported as state offline, not as an error. Returns the host as cerberus_host_get does.

name: cerberus_host_capacity
description: List the hosts that satisfy constraints, from recorded facts, in name order. Facts only: Cerberus does not rank, reserve or choose a host, and the caller decides placement. A host with no probe data, or data older than max_stale_age, is reported under unknown and never guessed to fit; call cerberus_host_probe on it for fresh facts. Set explain=true to also list excluded hosts with the reason for each.

disk_types.description: At least one recorded disk of one of these types.

explain.description: Also list excluded hosts with the reason for each.

free_memory_slots.description: At least this many empty memory slots (recorded).

free_storage_slots.description: Free storage slots required by kind, e.g. [{kind: nvme_m2, min: 1}]. A host whose slots are not recorded is unknown.

include_offline.description: Judge offline hosts on their last measurement (shown with its age) instead of excluding them.

labels.description: Labels that must all match exactly.

max_stale_age.description: Oldest probe a measured constraint is judged on, such as 10m. Default 5m.

min_disk_free.description: Minimum free disk on the data mount, in bytes or a size such as 50GB.

min_disk_size.description: At least one recorded disk at least this large.

min_memory_available.description: Minimum available memory, in bytes or a size such as 4GiB.

min_memory_total.description: Installed memory at least this (probed when fresh, else recorded), such as 16GiB.

min_memory_upgrade.description: Room to add at least this much memory: the recorded memory ceiling minus installed memory.

recent.description: Headroom held throughout a window: the host passes when its WORST sample in the window still meets every limit. Fewer than half the expected samples makes the host unknown. window is a duration up to 7d (default 15m).

require_tools.description: Probed tools that must be installed.

status_in.description: The monitor's status must be one of these.

name: cerberus_host_events
description: Host status-change events (status_changed: from, to, reason codes) after an event id, oldest first. Resume from last_id of the previous call; a gap means older events were pruned. Events carry status and reason codes only. Use cerberus_host_status for the details.

after_id.description: Return events after this id (0 for the oldest kept).

name: cerberus_host_status
description: Health of one host, or of every host when no name is given: online, degraded, offline or unknown, with reasons in plain words (disk_low, memory_low, load_high, probe_slow, unreachable, stale, ...), since when, the last good measurement, and the thresholds the status is derived from. A measurement older than three probe intervals reads unknown with its age. Facts only: not ranked, nothing reserved.

name.description: Host name; omit for every host.

name: cerberus_host_samples
description: A host's retained measurements (load, memory, disk, uptime, probe time) in time order, raw or as 5m, 1h or 1d rollups. since is an RFC 3339 time or a duration such as 6h; at most limit samples (default 500, the newest).

grain.description: raw (default) returns measurements; 5m, 1h and 1d return rollups: per bucket the sample count and min, mean and max of load, memory available, free disk and probe time.

since.description: RFC 3339 time or a duration such as 6h.

until.description: RFC 3339 time or a duration ago.

name: cerberus_host_monitor
description: What the host monitor is doing: whether it is on, its effective settings (intervals, jitter, backoff, concurrency, thresholds) and each monitored host's interval, last attempt and next probe.

name: cerberus_host_revision
description: The current revision of hosts.yaml. Pass it as `revision` on a host or component write.

name: cerberus_host_update
description: Change one host in hosts.yaml with a JSON merge patch (labels, notes, role, hardware, ceilings, storage_slots, ...): objects merge, null deletes a field, lists replace. The whole resulting file is validated first and a bad change writes nothing. Returns the changed fields (before/after) and the new revision. No credentials in any field.

acknowledged.description: The operator asked for this change.

approval_id.description: The approval id from an approval_pending answer, once your operator has approved it. Retry with exactly the same arguments; anything different is plan_stale.

create.description: Create the host when it does not exist.

patch.description: JSON merge patch of the host record.

revision.description: The hosts.yaml revision you read (cerberus_host_revision, or the revision in the last write's result). A write on a stale revision is refused and writes nothing.

name: cerberus_host_inventory
description: Collect a host's physical facts (make, model, serials, BIOS, CPU, memory layout, disks, NICs) over its ssh reach and record them. Runs a fixed read-only script, with sudo -n for root-only facts where the host allows it. Notes, storage_slots, vendor- or operator-sourced ceilings and components are kept. dry_run shows the change without writing. revision is optional here.

acknowledged.description: The operator asked for this change.

approval_id.description: The approval id from an approval_pending answer, once your operator has approved it. Retry with exactly the same arguments; anything different is plan_stale.

dry_run.description: Collect and show what would change; write nothing.

revision.description: Optional: the hosts.yaml revision you read.
